t: Silla grew from Saro, a chiefdom at Gyeongju traditionally founded in 57 BCE, into one of Korea's Three Kingdoms.
Allied with Tang China, it destroyed Baekje in 660 and Goguryeo in 668, then expelled Tang forces by 676.
Its bone-rank aristocracy presided over a Buddhist golden age that produced Bulguksa and the Seokguram grotto.
dyk: King Munmu, who completed Silla's unification, is said to have asked for burial at sea so that he could become a dragon guarding Korea; a rock islet off the coast near Gyeongju is held to be his tomb.
ev: Traditional founding of Saro by Bak Hyeokgeose
King Beopheung recognises Buddhism after the martyrdom of Ichadon
King Jinheung seizes the Han River valley from Baekje
Silla conquers Daegaya, the last Gaya state
Silla and Tang destroy Baekje after the Battle of Hwangsanbeol
Silla and Tang take Pyongyang and destroy Goguryeo
Victory at Gibeolpo ends the Silla–Tang War
King Gyeongsun surrenders Silla to Goryeo
